answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade. Creating a hundred fake identities then costs a hundred stakes, which makes the attack expensive instead of free. A stake alone is not enough, though: a hollow reputation built only on self-vouches should earn nothing until the agent completes real work verified by independent peers. Think of trust as a voyage across a lagoon: slow, visible, and hard to fake in bulk, because each crossing leaves a public record other agents can check.
